eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket heavily favors Warsaw highs of 22–23°C on May 11, driven by the latest ECMWF ensemble and IMGW forecasts showing mean maximum temperatures in that narrow band amid a high-pressure ridge promoting diurnal heating after a cool spell. Recent IMGW observations note spring variability, with early-week peaks near 27°C giving way to 13–14°C on May 8 under persistent cloud cover, but models now project partial clearing and light southerly winds aiding a rebound. Differentiating factors include afternoon cloud timing—persistent overcast caps peaks at 21–22°C in cooler ensemble members, while earlier breaks allow 23–24°C in warmer outliers—reflecting inherent short-range forecast uncertainty. New ECMWF and GFS runs expected overnight could refine this, alongside IMGW hourly updates. Historical May 11 averages hover near 19°C, underscoring the mild anomaly.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket favors a 31°C high in Beijing on May 11 at 46.5% implied probability, driven by the UK Met Office forecast of 31°C under sunny conditions contrasting the China Meteorological Administration's (CMA) more conservative 30°C outlook with partial cloudiness and light southeast winds. This positioning reflects May 10's observed peak of 32.4°C at Beijing Capital International Airport—exceeding early projections—and a warming trend with recent highs around 30°C earlier in the month, amplified by seasonal southerly flow and Beijing's urban heat island effect. International model ensembles like ECMWF suggest potential for 31–32°C if afternoon clearing occurs, though cloud development could cap temperatures at 30°C; final CMA observations post-midnight May 12 will resolve the market amid typical short-range forecast uncertainty.

Gelabert International Airport on May 11. NOAA global model updates expected later today could refine this; historical May averages hover around 32°C, underscoring inherent short-term forecast variability.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices a tight race among 29–31°C for Guangzhou's highest temperature on May 11, driven by the latest China Meteorological Administration and global model forecasts projecting peaks near 29–30°C amid lingering cloud cover from recent thundershowers. Persistent overcast skies over the past week capped May 6–10 highs at 26–27°C, suppressing solar insolation despite humid subtropical conditions favoring seasonal averages around 29–30°C. Differentiating factors include afternoon cloud break probabilities—ECMWF and GFS ensembles show slight divergence, with partial clearing potentially boosting to 31°C via enhanced shortwave radiation, while sustained convection favors 29°C. Official observations from Baiyun Airport will resolve the market tomorrow, with updates expected overnight.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects high uncertainty in Singapore's peak temperature for May 12, with implied probabilities tightly clustered around 29–33°C amid inter-monsoon conditions featuring light, variable winds that foster daytime heat buildup. The National Environment Agency's fortnightly outlook for late April through mid-May forecasts daily maximums of 33–35°C on most days, tempered by frequent afternoon thundery showers that often cap peaks through cloud cover and precipitation—evident in recent late-April highs reaching 35.5°C before shower suppression. Differentiating factors include shower onset timing (midday convection lowers odds for 32°C+), localized gust fronts from Sumatra squalls, and urban heat effects at Changi Airport station. NEA's daily updates through May 11–12 will refine model consensus on these convective patterns.
